knowledge_gaps: The proposed comparison identifies the effect of dropout under the curriculum, but cannot distinguish generic regularization from the benefit of protecting recent context. A count-matched random-position dropout control would help; reduced sensitivity to deleted older items alone would not establish improved relevance.

PAD holes preserve absolute positions only if the actual BERT4Rec implementation uses fixed position indices and does not compact valid tokens. Attention masking, positional indexing, and any nested-tensor optimization need verification. Changing these behaviors would require consistent predictor generation.

Reproducibility remains incomplete: the report lacks the corrected baseline's concrete configuration, remaining GPU budget, per-arm resource allocation, augmentation-stream reset policy across categories, and checkpoint-selection details. It should also record eligible positions, realized deletions, unchanged-example rates, and history-length strata.

The 0.5375 versus 0.5425 difference is descriptive historical evidence, not an isolated curriculum effect. Under the stated evaluator, a macro difference of 0.005 corresponds to four net validation hits across 800 users; paired outcomes and selection history are needed to assess it.

Originality 4 and difficulty 3 are provisional. Related sequence-augmentation methods need comparison, and integration difficulty depends on PAD-hole compatibility. Potential 7 is optimistic while serving parity and recency dependence remain unmeasured.
